description: Consolidate the two independent PresenterSettings writers into ONE PresenterSettingsService (Core), file-backed for now (presenter-settings.json), removing the double-writer hazard BEFORE the backing store changes. The LIVE writer today is PresenterIntegration.SavePresenterSettings (PresenterIntegration.cs:420-438, wired as the OperatorWindow save callback at :252, which also calls ApplyDisplaySettings at :436). The reader is MainWindow.LoadPresenterSettings (MainWindow.xaml.cs:1512-1527, uses PropertyNameCaseInsensitive). MainWindow's static SavePresenterSettings (MainWindow.xaml.cs:1529-1535) is VERIFIED DEAD CODE (grep finds no caller). The new service owns load+save with ONE canonical JsonSerializerOptions. This FEAT leaves the app fully buildable and behavior-identical; it does NOT touch SQLite. Depends on nothing; FEAT-002 depends on it.
steps: Create WorshipPlayer.Core/Services/PresenterSettingsService.cs mirroring SettingsService.cs. Public API: ctor PresenterSettingsService(string settingsPath); PresenterSettings Settings { get; private set; } = new(); Task LoadAsync(); Task SaveAsync(). Use canonical options: new JsonSerializerOptions { WriteIndented = true, Converters = { new JsonStringEnumConverter() }, PropertyNameCaseInsensitive = true } — a strict superset of all three existing paths (indented writes + case-insensitive reads from MainWindow.LoadPresenterSettings + enums-as-strings parity matching SongUsageService.cs:34-38). LoadAsync: if the file exists, read + deserialize into Settings, falling back to new PresenterSettings() on missing-or-malformed (match the try/catch leniency of MainWindow.LoadPresenterSettings:1515-1526); do NOT auto-write a file on missing (presenter settings never auto-created one). SaveAsync: ensure parent dir, serialize Settings, File.WriteAllTextAsync.

In WorshipPlayer.UI/Views/MainWindow.xaml.cs: where LoadPresenterSettings() is called (:175), instead construct a PresenterSettingsService against Path.Combine(appFolder,"presenter-settings.json"), await LoadAsync(), store it in a new MainWindow field (e.g. _presenterSettingsService) for reuse, and pass .Settings into the PresenterIntegration ctor (:176). Delete the dead static SavePresenterSettings (:1529-1535); delete the now-unused LoadPresenterSettings (:1512-1527) and GetPresenterSettingsPath (:1506-1510) since the service replaces them.

In WorshipPlayer.UI/Services/PresenterIntegration.cs: add the PresenterSettingsService to the ctor (:71-79) alongside the existing PresenterSettings param (the in-memory instance the engine/display code mutates stays). Change the private SavePresenterSettings (:420-438) so persistence delegates to the injected PresenterSettingsService (set its Settings to the passed settings, then call SaveAsync()) — remove the inline JsonSerializer.Serialize + File.WriteAllText block — while KEEPING the ApplyDisplaySettings(settings) call (:436) and the OperatorWindow save-callback wiring (:252) unchanged. Update the MainWindow construction (:176) to pass the service into the ctor.

Add WorshipPlayer.Tests/PresenterSettingsServiceTests.cs (xUnit, temp-folder pattern like AutoAdvanceSettingsPersistenceTests:19-27 Dispose). Cover: (a) no file -> defaults (StageServerEnabled true, StageServerPort 5055, ScriptureShowReference true); (b) save -> reload through a fresh service instance preserves additive E5/J4 fields (ScriptureShowReference, ScriptureShowTranslationName, CcliLicenseNumber) and NDI/stage-server/remote/shortcut fields; (c) malformed file -> defaults, no throw; (d) single-save-path: save via the service and reload via the service yields identical values (proves no divergent writer).
acceptance_criteria: WorshipPlayer.Core/Services/PresenterSettingsService.cs exists with Settings property + LoadAsync + SaveAsync and a single canonical JsonSerializerOptions.

No code path other than PresenterSettingsService writes presenter-settings.json: the dead MainWindow static SavePresenterSettings is gone and PresenterIntegration.SavePresenterSettings delegates to the service (ApplyDisplaySettings still invoked).
MainWindow loads presenter settings via the service and injects the service into PresenterIntegration.
Running `dotnet test WorshipBacktrackPlayer.sln --filter FullyQualifiedName~PresenterSettingsServiceTests` passes all new tests, including the single-save-path and E5/J4-survival tests.
verification: dotnet build WorshipBacktrackPlayer.sln  -> 0 errors (4 known pre-existing warnings OK).
dotnet test WorshipBacktrackPlayer.sln --filter FullyQualifiedName~PresenterSettingsStageServerTests  -> still pass (model parity unaffected).
findings:
DONE. Build 0 errors (4 known warnings). PresenterSettingsServiceTests 4/4 pass; PresenterSettingsStageServerTests 4/4 still pass.

FINAL SIGNATURES (FEAT-002 will retarget the backing store):
- WorshipPlayer.Core/Services/PresenterSettingsService.cs: ctor PresenterSettingsService(string settingsPath); public PresenterSettings Settings { get; set; } = new(); Task LoadAsync(); Task SaveAsync(). Canonical JsonSerializerOptions = { WriteIndented = true, Converters = { new JsonStringEnumConverter() }, PropertyNameCaseInsensitive = true }.
- DEVIATION from the 'mirror SettingsService exactly' guidance: Settings uses a PUBLIC setter (not `private set` like SettingsService.Settings). Reason: Step 3 mandates PresenterIntegration.SavePresenterSettings set the service's Settings to the operator-passed instance, and the save callback (OperatorWindow/DisplaySettingsWindow) may pass a DIFFERENT PresenterSettings reference than the one injected at startup, so a settable property is required for the single-writer delegation. FEAT-002: when migrating to SQLite you may keep the public setter or switch to a (string path, string? databasePath = null) ctor like MediaLibraryService — the setter does not block that.
- LoadAsync does NOT auto-write on missing file (presenter settings never auto-created one); SettingsService.LoadAsync DOES auto-write on missing — do not copy that behavior into the presenter path. Malformed/missing => defaults, never throws.

CONSTRUCTION SITES (for FEAT-002 ctor changes):
- WorshipPlayer.UI/Views/MainWindow.xaml.cs: new field `private PresenterSettingsService _presenterSettingsService = null!;`. In MainWindow_Loaded it is built as `new PresenterSettingsService(Path.Combine(appFolder, "presenter-settings.json"))`, awaited LoadAsync(), and its .Settings injected into the PresenterIntegration ctor. appFolder = AppDomain.CurrentDomain.BaseDirectory; sibling app.db path used by the SQLite services is Path.Combine(appFolder, "app.db"). Dead static SavePresenterSettings, unused LoadPresenterSettings, and GetPresenterSettingsPath were all DELETED from MainWindow.
- WorshipPlayer.UI/Services/PresenterIntegration.cs: ctor now takes PresenterSettingsService as a NEW param positioned AFTER presenterSettings and BEFORE songManager -> (AudioEngine, MidiCueService, AppSettings, PresenterSettings, PresenterSettingsService, SongManager). Stored in readonly field _presenterSettingsService. Private SavePresenterSettings now does `_presenterSettingsService.Settings = settings; _presenterSettingsService.SaveAsync().GetAwaiter().GetResult();` inside try/catch, then still calls ApplyDisplaySettings(settings). OperatorWindow save-callback wiring at the OpenPresenterWindow site is unchanged. The in-memory _presenterSettings instance the engine/display code mutates is unchanged.
- NOTE for FEAT-002: SaveAsync is invoked synchronously via GetAwaiter().GetResult() from the UI save callback. If FEAT-002's SQLite SaveAsync does real async I/O this stays fine (no SynchronizationContext deadlock risk here since it is a fire-after-settings-change path), but keep SaveAsync self-contained.
